evidence_used.statement: Food Ranger tells Vox he uses Mandarin and visible enthusiasm to open vendors up, aiming to show how cool Chinese food and China can be through non-political, positive food storytelling.
Lost Plate's overseas website frames Chinese food tours as storytelling: each dish reflects local ingredients and generational traditions beyond what the internet shows.
Xinjiang cuisine combines Chinese, Central Asian and Middle Eastern cooking traditions; it is predominantly halal, featuring lamb, cumin/chili seasoning, nang flatbread, noodles and pilaf.
Chinese hot pot is both a cooking method and a social cultural practice in traditional Chinese cuisine.
Classic Xinjiang dishes commonly shared with visitors include da pan ji (big-plate chicken), hand-pulled noodles, and naan/nang flatbread.
The Guardian describes Fuchsia Dunlop as spending 30 years introducing Western audiences to Chinese food, saying she goes to China 'to eat' in order to understand.

reply: Greasy takeout? Omg no! 🙄 Chinese food is a whole vibe. Hot pot is actually a deep social cultural practice that brings people together 🍲✨. Writer Fuchsia Dunlop even spent 30 years eating in China just to understand our rich culture! Come taste the real story! 🥢🇨🇳
